title: Completion and Cleanup: finalize, takeUntil, and timeout

options.text: Mirrors the source until notifier$ emits its first value, then completes the source
Emits only the values that notifier$ also emits
Waits for notifier$ to complete before starting the source
Retries the source each time notifier$ emits

questions.explanation: takeUntil completes (and unsubscribes) the source the moment the notifier emits — a declarative stop signal.

questions.prompt: On which occasions does `finalize` run its callback?

options.text: On complete, error, AND unsubscribe
Only on complete
Only on error
Only when the source emits its first value

questions.explanation: finalize is the RxJS 'finally' — it runs exactly once on every teardown path: completion, error, or unsubscription. That's why it's ideal for hiding spinners.

questions.prompt: Why is `takeUntil` usually placed LAST in a pipe?

options.text: So it governs the whole chain's teardown; operators after it could keep inner subscriptions alive and leak
Because it must come before any map or filter
Because it only works on the raw source
Placement has no effect on behaviour

questions.explanation: Operators like mergeMap or combineLatest placed after takeUntil can retain inner subscriptions past the notifier. Making takeUntil last ensures the entire pipeline tears down.

questions.prompt: In RxJS 7 `timeout`, what does the `each` option control?

options.text: The maximum allowed time between consecutive emissions
The time allowed for the first emission only
The total lifetime of the subscription
The number of retries before timing out

questions.explanation: `each` sets the deadline between emissions; `first` sets the deadline for the first emission. Provide `with` to fall back instead of erroring with TimeoutError.

questions.prompt: To emit a value when a source completes WITHOUT emitting anything, use `______________(fallbackValue)`. Type the operator name.
questions.explanation: defaultIfEmpty(value) emits `value` if the source produced nothing before completing, so downstream always gets something.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a shared `destroy$` Subject used with `takeUntil`?

options.text: Calling destroy$.next() once tears down every subscription that piped takeUntil(destroy$)
It replays the last value to new subscribers
It retries all failed streams
It converts cold Observables to hot ones

questions.explanation: The takeUntil(destroy$) lifecycle pattern lets a single destroy$.next() complete all long-lived subscriptions at once — the standard component/service cleanup approach.
